chunks: And from him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abu Hammam, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Ghazwan, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Above every person of goodness is goodness, until he is killed in the cause of Allah; so when he is killed in the cause of Allah, there is no goodness above him. And above every person of disobedience is disobedience, until he kills one of his two parents; so when he kills one of his two parents, there is no disobedience above him.

key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: In the cause of Allah (often referring to jihad or martyrdom)

ai.seo_question: What is the highest level of goodness and the highest level of disobedience in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes a definitive hierarchy of virtue (birr) and vice (uquq), positioning martyrdom in Allah’s cause as the apex of goodness and parental homicide as the ultimate peak of disobedience. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of piety from general righteousness to the highest spiritual station, while also highlighting the gravity of filial piety by using its violation as the baseline for maximum vice.
